title: Jordan Block Counts from the Generalized-Eigenspace Dimension Tower
description: Recovers the Jordan block counts per size from the generalized-eigenspace dimension tower d_k(μ) = dim ker((f − μ)^k), with no explicit Jordan basis (which Mathlib 4.26.0 lacks). The mathematical core is the CONCAVITY of the tower, d_{k+2} + d_k ≤ 2 d_{k+1}, which makes the exact-size block counts genuine non-negative integers. Concavity is proved cleanly by exhibiting the antitone chain of image submodules N^k(ker N^{k+1}), whose dimensions are the successive differences d_{k+1} − d_k. Block counts of size ≥ j (Weyr characteristic) and exact size j are defined off the tower, with telescoping to the algebraic multiplicity, total count = geometric multiplicity, and a full eigenvalue interface to Module.End.genEigenspace. 16 theorems, 4 definitions, 0 axioms, 0 sorries.

overview.historicalContext: The grandparent entry (cayley-hamilton-minpoly-oq-01) axiomatized the Jordan-canonical-form product formula minpoly = ∏ (X − μ)^{e_μ}; the parent (cayley-hamilton-minpoly-oq-01-oq-01) proved it outright from generalized-eigenspace theory alone, and flagged as an explicit open question the recovery of the full Jordan block count per size from the same dimension tower. This entry answers that question. The classical fact — Eduard Weyr's 1885 characteristic — is that the number of Jordan blocks of size ≥ j at an eigenvalue equals d_j − d_{j-1}, where d_k = dim ker((f − μ)^k), so the number of blocks of exact size j is 2 d_j − d_{j-1} − d_{j+1}. For these to be genuine counts one needs the nullity tower to be concave. Mathlib 4.26.0 provides no explicit Jordan block matrix with a labeled basis, so the concavity is proved here directly with rank–nullity and submodule dimension calculus.
overview.problemStatement: Recover the Jordan block counts per size — blocks of size ≥ j and blocks of exact size j — from the generalized-eigenspace dimension tower d_k(μ) = dim(genEigenspace f μ k) = dim ker((f − μ)^k), and prove the concavity d_{k+2} + d_k ≤ 2 d_{k+1} that makes these counts well-defined non-negative integers, all without constructing a Jordan basis.
overview.text: Work with a general endomorphism N of a finite-dimensional space (take N = f − μ•1 per eigenvalue) and the nullity tower d_k = dim ker(N^k). The kernels form an increasing chain, so d_k is monotone. Restrict N^k to the subspace ker(N^{k+1}): its range is the image submodule P_k = N^k(ker N^{k+1}), and its kernel is ker(N^{k+1}) ∩ ker(N^k) = ker(N^k); rank–nullity therefore gives d_{k+1} = dim P_k + d_k, so dim P_k = d_{k+1} − d_k is exactly the number of blocks of size ≥ k+1. The decisive step is that N maps P_{k+1} into P_k (if v ∈ ker N^{k+2} then N^{k+1}v = N^k(Nv) with Nv ∈ ker N^{k+1}), so the P_k are an antitone chain and dim P_{k+1} ≤ dim P_k. Combined with the two rank–nullity identities this yields concavity d_{k+2} + d_k ≤ 2 d_{k+1}. The block-count functions blocksAtLeast (d_j − d_{j-1}, the Weyr characteristic) and blocksExact (its successive difference) then telescope to d_m, give the total count = dim ker N (geometric multiplicity) at size ≥ 1, and satisfy #{size = k+1} = 2 d_{k+1} − d_k − d_{k+2}. Finally genEigenspace_nat identifies d_k(N = f − μ) with dim(genEigenspace f μ k), so every statement transports to each eigenvalue of f.
overview.proofStrategy: Prove monotonicity of ker(N^k) directly. Establish nullity_succ by applying finrank_range_add_finrank_ker to (N^k).domRestrict (ker N^{k+1}), identifying the range with the image submodule via range_domRestrict and the restricted kernel with ker(N^k) via ker_comp, map_comap_subtype, finrank_map_subtype_eq, and inf_of_le_right. Prove jordanImage_antitone by an explicit membership chase using pow_succ and Module.End.mul_apply. Derive concavity by feeding the two nullity_succ instances and finrank_mono of the antitone inclusion to omega. Define the block-count functions, prove their telescoping, antitonicity, and tower-coordinate formulas, and bridge to genEigenspace via genEigenspace_nat.
keyInsights: The Jordan block counts per size need no Jordan basis — the increasing kernel tower and rank–nullity suffice, exactly as the parent entry recovered the largest block size spectrally
The number of blocks of size ≥ k+1 is dim(N^k(ker N^{k+1})), a concrete image submodule, and equals the tower difference d_{k+1} − d_k
Concavity d_{k+2} + d_k ≤ 2 d_{k+1} is the statement that the block counts are non-negative, and it follows from a single antitone inclusion N·P_{k+1} ⊆ P_k
Restricting N^k to ker(N^{k+1}) turns the abstract successive-difference into a rank–nullity identity that omega can combine

genEigenspace_nat is the one bridge lemma: it turns the abstract nullity tower of f − μ into the generalized-eigenspace dimension tower, transporting concavity and all block-count formulas to every eigenvalue
prerequisites: Generalized eigenspaces: Module.End.genEigenspace and genEigenspace_nat (genEigenspace f μ k = ker((f − μ•1)^k))

conclusion.summary: The Jordan block counts per size are recovered from the generalized-eigenspace dimension tower with 0 axioms and 0 sorries: blocks of size ≥ j equal d_j − d_{j-1}, blocks of exact size j equal 2 d_j − d_{j-1} − d_{j+1}, they telescope to the algebraic multiplicity and sum (at size ≥ 1) to the geometric multiplicity, and the tower is concave d_{k+2} + d_k ≤ 2 d_{k+1}. 16 theorems, 4 definitions, 284 lines. No Jordan basis is used — only rank–nullity and submodule dimension calculus.
conclusion.implications: This closes the parent entry's stated open question and completes the spectral picture of the Jordan structure: the grandparent's product formula recovers the largest block size per eigenvalue, and this entry recovers the entire block-size distribution, all without the explicit Jordan block matrix that Mathlib still lacks. The concavity proof (an antitone chain of image submodules) and the rank–nullity level identity are reusable, eigenvalue-agnostic ingredients suitable for upstreaming as the Weyr characteristic.
openQuestions: Package the block counts into a formal partition (the Weyr / conjugate-Young-diagram invariant) and prove it equals the Jordan block-size multiset once Mathlib gains an explicit Jordan basis
Upstream nullity_concave and nullity_succ as the Weyr characteristic of a nilpotent endomorphism to Mathlib
Relate blocksExact for f − μ to the exponent maxGenEigenspaceIndex f μ (largest block size) proved in the parent entry, showing the top nonzero block count sits at that index
